section_summary: Pages 109–118 conclude a first-person account of Japanese Communist Party members’ imprisonment, wartime detention, and release in October 1945. The remaining pages contain 1948 U.S. diplomatic reporting on attacks against communist leaders, the party’s electoral prospects and propaganda, and an extended assessment of its political, covert, and international capabilities. The assessment’s enclosed memorandum continues beyond page 143.

subfiles.title: Account of imprisonment and release of Japanese communist leaders
subfiles.about: Shiga recounts communist prisoners’ treatment, wartime detention, and release after Japan’s surrender.
subfiles.summary: The narrative describes pressure on prisoners to renounce communism, severe conditions and forced labor at Hakodate and Chiba, and preferential treatment for those who recanted. It follows transfers through Kosuge and precautionary detention, wartime air raids, political discussions among imprisoned communists, and journalists’ discovery of the prisoners before their October 1945 release.

subfiles.title: Attempted Assassination of Tokuda Kyuichi, Secretary General of the Japan Communist Party
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Koga Ichiro’s attack on Tokuda and the political reaction in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Sebald describes communist and union denunciations of the attack, Koga’s background and anti-communist affiliation, and the party’s effort to link the incident to government policy. He notes no evidence that an organization helped plan it.

subfiles.title: Message to the Japanese Communist Party concerning the Tokuda attack
subfiles.about: Reports a communist message acknowledging a communication about the attack on Tokuda.
subfiles.summary: Noisy text records a party secretariat message and notes a discrepancy between its stated and received dates.

subfiles.title: Japanese Communist Party prospects in the next Diet
subfiles.about: Relays a Central News Agency item assessing possible gains by Japanese communists.
subfiles.summary: The item links growing communist sympathy to anti-occupation sentiment, fear of Soviet power, repatriation, and labor disputes. It expects limited gains in a future Diet while doubting the party will gain substantial near-term national influence.

subfiles.title: Pan-Asiatic Communist Bloc
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Compares Chinese left-wing writing with Japanese communist propaganda and alleges regional coordination.
subfiles.summary: Sebald identifies shared themes of American imperialism, racial independence, and resistance across Asia. He argues that similar propaganda in China, Japan, and Korea may reflect covert Cominform coordination.

subfiles.title: Formation of a League for Defense of Democracy
subfiles.about: Relays a report that Japanese communists and the socialist left are forming a political league.
subfiles.summary: A press report says the proposed league invited democratic parties and worker, peasant, and business groups.

subfiles.title: Reported attempt to assassinate Ito Ritsu
subfiles.about: Relays Soviet press accounts of a failed attempt against Japanese communist Ito Ritsu.
subfiles.summary: The report attributes the alleged plot to a rival party figure and notes Akahata’s criticism of the Ashida Cabinet.

subfiles.title: The Communist Potential in Japan
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards and summarizes Charles Nelson Spinks’s study of the Japan Communist Party.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reviews the party’s modest electoral strength and disciplined leadership, then emphasizes its alleged infiltration of unions and other groups, covert units, espionage, and international liaison. He judges near-term electoral success unlikely but considers its longer-term subversive capacity significant.

subfiles.title: The Communist Potential in Japan
subfiles.about: Analyzes party membership, sympathizers, and election performance as part of a longer study.
subfiles.summary: The contents page outlines overt, covert, and international sections. The pages present estimates of official and hidden party membership, discuss the influence of communist sympathizers, and assess results in the 1946 and 1947 national and local elections. The memorandum argues that disciplined activism gives the party influence beyond its small vote share. It continues after page 143.
